attribution.note: Marcus states the proposition in his own voice.

semantics.note: The normalization faithfully isolates the regulatory claim without importing the separate revenue assertion.

contract.note: Reading 'any regulation' as a blanket exemption is ordinary and fair. The contemporary policy window is reasonable. A narrower reading restricted to foundation-model obligations could change the assessment.

evidence.note: Google's contemporaneous policy disclosure advocates regulation and substantive legal protections. It contradicts the blanket public-policy attribution, though it cannot establish private intentions.

The industry statement seeks limited foundation-model duties but expressly supports AI Act regulation of high-risk uses and transparency standards. That affirmative support contradicts exemption from all binding regulation.

reviews.rationale: Under the fair plain reading, the claim attributes a blanket regulatory-exemption objective to big tech. Google's proposal and the industry statement support regulatory obligations. Lobbying to narrow foundation-model rules supports Marcus's narrower concern but does not establish the blanket claim. These disclosures establish expressed positions, not undisclosed motives.
